entry.title: MB26 can't create outbound deliveries for serialized materials on maintenance order reservations
entry.content:
Hi experts,

We're on SAP S/4HANA 2023 FPS01 with embedded EWM and PM–EWM integration. All storage locations for maintenance order components are EWM-managed.

Requirement When a maintenance order is released, an outbound delivery should be created automatically for its component reservations. The warehouse worker then picks and posts goods issue in EWM as usual. Only the delivery creation step needs to be automated.

Our plan Schedule MB26 as a background job to create the deliveries, with EWM capturing the serial number during picking.

The problem For serialized materials, MB26 stops with a hard error before any delivery is created:

Material 100045 requires serial numbers

KBA 1767555 says MB26 doesn't support serial numbers. It suggests using MIGO or excluding serialized materials in MB26 (Note 630888). MIGO is a dialog transaction, so it doesn't meet the automation requirement.

Serial number setup:

  • S/4 serial number profile ZSP1: MMSL = 03 (obligatory), SDLS = 03 (obligatory)
  • EWM serial number requirement: warehouse number level

Questions

  1. Is there a standard SAP way to create outbound deliveries automatically for maintenance order reservations with serialized materials on EWM-managed storage locations?
  2. If MMSL is set to optional (02) in the S/4 profile, will MB26 create the delivery and leave serial number capture to EWM? Have you seen any side effects?
  3. How have others handled this scenario in S/4HANA with EWM?

Thanks in advance.

entry.title: Why You Should Migrate Cost Center Groups to Global Hierarchies
entry.content:
In an earlier release of SAP S4/HANA Cloud Public Edition, the Manage Global Hierarchies (ID: F2918) was introduced as a central place for maintaining various hierarchy types, including cost center hierarchies. One of its key purposes is to replace the legacy Manage Cost Center Groups app (ID: F1024).

We strongly recommend migrating your cost center groups to Manage Global Hierarchies to take advantage of its enhanced capabilities, ensure business continuity, and future-proof your processes.

In this blog, we’ll explore the benefits of the new app, compare it with the classic app, and guide you through the migration process.

The Traditional Way: Manage Cost Center Groups

For years, cost center groups were created and edited in the classic app Manage Cost Center Groups. Cost center standard hierarchy could also be edited there.  

The following graphic provides an overview of the app user interface:

To use a cost center group in reporting, the following steps are required after creating or editing the group:
Step 1: Mark the hierarchy as report-relevant
Open the Set Report Relevancy app (ID: F5295) and mark the hierarchy as report-relevant.
Step 2: Replicate the hierarchy
Use the Replicate Runtime Hierarchy (ID: F1478) app to replicate set-based hierarchies to back-end database tables. If this replication is not performed, then these hierarchies cannot be used in reporting.

For more information, refer to the following documentation on the SAP Help Portal:

  • Manage Cost Center Groups (Deprecated)
  • Set Report Relevancy
  • Replicate Runtime Hierarchy 

The New Way: Manage Global Hierarchies

The Manage Global Hierarchies app introduced in a recent release, modernizes cost center hierarchy maintenance. Aside from viewing, creating, and editing cost center hierarchies as in the classic app, the new app enables you to quickly create hierarchies by importing or copying from existing hierarchies in the event of structure changes or changing reporting needs. Additionally, you can check change logs and maintain node texts in multiple languages for applicable hierarchy types. 

Key Features

  • View and filter existing hierarchies by criteria such as hierarchy type, status, and validity timeframe
  • Create, copy, edit hierarchies, and manage their validity timeframes
  • Activate or deactivate hierarchies for runtime use
  • Export, edit, and import hierarchies via a spreadsheet
  • Import hierarchies created with compatible applications
  • View change logs of applicable hierarchy types
  • Maintain node texts in multiple languages for applicable hierarchy types
  • After being activated, hierarchies can be consumed in all analytical reports
  • Reuse Hierarchies in Group-Related Apps

The following graphic provides an overview of the app user interface:

For more information, refer to Manage Global Hierarchies  on the SAP Help Portal.  

Why Migrate?

Compared with the Manage Cost Center Groups app, which is used to maintain set-based groups, Manage Global Hierarchies provides a unified solution for managing various hierarchy types within a single application. In addition, thanks to the SAP Fiori UI technology, hierarchies can be exported to, edited in, and imported from spreadsheets, significantly improving maintenance efficiency. Furthermore, the global hierarchy framework simplifies the consumption of hierarchies across analytical applications and reports, enabling more consistent and seamless reporting experiences.

We strongly recommend using the new Manage Global Hierarchies app to maintain cost centers. Rest assured, existing cost center groups created in the classic app can be seamlessly migrated to the global hierarchies framework. We encourage you to do the migration as soon as possible for the following reasons:

  • The new app provides more robust functionality and greater flexibility to meet your business needs that are unavailable in the classic app.
  • The classic app is planned to be deprecated in the future.
  • New features are only delivered to the new app.

For more information, refer to Set-Based Groups versus Global Hierarchies. 

How to Migrate: Step-by-Step

Migrating your existing cost center groups is simple and efficient. Follow the steps below using the Migrate Set-Based Groups to Global Hierarchies app (ID: F6228) . 

1. Open the app, choose Hierarchy Type 0101 (Cost Center Group).

2. Select the old hierarchy of the cost center group you’d like to migrate, and choose the Migrate button. Take 8765 as an example.

3. In the migration details page, choose Migrate. 

4. You will then be navigated to the page below, which confirms that the hierarchy has been migrated to the Manage Global Hierarchies app.

5. To confirm the migration, open the Manage Global Hierarchies app and check the details of 8765.

6. Repeat the steps above to migrate all cost center groups.

After completing the migration, click the Mark as Completed button in the aforementioned migration app to finalize the process and confirm that the cost center type has been successfully and fully migrated.

For more information, refer to the following documentation: How to Migrate Cost Center Groups to Global Hierarchies 

Special Case: Cost Center Standard Hierarchy

Among all cost center hierarchies, the Cost Center Standard Hierarchy (Hierarchy ID 1) has special behavior:
• Hierarchy ID 1 is reserved for the standard hierarchy. All cost centers are automatically assigned to this hierarchy upon creation.
• The Standard Hierarchy Node field in the Manage Cost Centers app is bidirectionally synchronized with the structure maintained in Manage Global Hierarchies.
• Because all cost centers are automatically assigned upon creation, the Unassigned tab is always empty for Hierarchy ID 1.
Note: Before activating cost center standard hierarchy 1, ensure that all cost centers have been assigned to it. Failure to do so will prevent the activation of the standard hierarchy. If you encounter this issue, check the Unassigned tab. If there are any cost centers listed, assign them to the standard hierarchy.

For more information, see Cost Center Standard Hierarchies on the SAP Help Portal.  

Final Thoughts

The Manage Global Hierarchies app offers enhanced functionality and eliminates the need for separate report relevancy and replication steps before cost center hierarchies can be used for reporting. As the Manage Cost Center Groups app has been deprecated, migrating your cost center groups to Manage Global Hierarchies helps ensure business continuity while enabling you to take advantage of its new capabilities.

We hope this blog has helped you better understand the transition process. If you have any questions or need further assistance, feel free to leave a comment below.

entry.title: What's New in SAP Integrated Product Development: Sep'26 Update
entry.content:
What’s New for SAP Integrated Product Development

Welcome to the September 2026 blog! This update introduces powerful enhancements designed to accelerate innovation, strengthen collaboration, and improve efficiency across the product lifecycle. With expanded engineering capabilities and deeper integration with SAP and partner solutions, it further enhances how teams work together—from concept through manufacturing and beyond. 

Change Management

Visualize Problem Report and Change Process Status Progress

You can now visualize the status network in the Progress tab of the Manage Problem Reports and Manage Change Processes apps. The graphical view provides a clear overview of the workflow, highlighting completed, current, and upcoming statuses. It also dynamically displays all available status transitions, making it easier to track progress and understand the workflow at a glance.

[Shows an overview of the changes and UI, as outlined in the text.]

To learn more about the feature, see Progress in Change Processes, Progress in Problem Reports.  

Maintain Change Request Relevance for Design Item and Document Objects

You can now maintain additional Change Request Relevance values for Design Item and Document objects. The available options include New Version, Change, and Not Relevant, providing greater flexibility in defining how these objects are handled within a Change Request process.

[Shows an overview of the changes and UI, as outlined in the text.]

To learn more about the feature, see Change Request.  

Add Document Business Objects to Change Management Apps

You can now add the Document business object across several Change Management apps, extending document support within change processes. This includes the Reference Item section in the Manage Problem Reports app, the Change Request section in the Manage Change Processes app, and the Object Types section in the Configure Change Process Types app. These enhancements provide greater flexibility in managing documents throughout the change management lifecycle.

[Shows an overview of the changes and UI, as outlined in the text.]

To learn more about the feature, see  Change Request ,Reference Item, Object Types. 

Configure Workflow-Based Email Notifications

You can now integrate SAP Build Process Automation with Change Management to configure automated email notifications for processors whenever the status of their assigned change processes or problem reports changes. This integration helps keep processors informed of important status updates, improving visibility and streamlining change management workflows.

Collaboration

Linking Change Processes as Standard Reference Objects

You can now add Change Processes as standard reference objects directly from the My Collaborations app. This enhancement allows you to manage change-related activities with internal and external stakeholders within a collaboration, while ensuring end-to-end traceability between change processes and collaborative tasks. This enables better coordination and visibility throughout the change management lifecycle.

[Shows an overview of the changes and UI, as outlined in the text.]

To learn more about the feature, see Reference Objects.

Export Collaboration List Data to Excel

You can now export the complete Collaboration List page data to Excel directly from the My Collaborations app using a dedicated UI button. The export includes all attributes displayed on the list page and covers only the collaborations you are authorized to access. This enhancement makes it easier to perform offline analysis, share reports, and leverage collaboration data in external reporting tools.

[Shows an overview of the changes and UI, as outlined in the text.]

To learn more about the feature, see Working with Collaborations.

Common Functions

New SAP-Defined Link Types tab

You can now access a new SAP-Defined Link Types tab in the Configure Link Types screen, alongside the existing customer-defined link types. This tab provides a read-only view of predefined link types delivered by SAP, offering greater transparency into system-defined relationships. Customers can continue to create and manage their own link types, while SAP-defined link types support predefined business processes and are seamlessly handled at runtime.

Formulation

Specification Price as a new price source for Estimated Price calculations

You can now use Specification Price as a new price source for Estimated Price calculations in SAP IPD.

In the Configure Recipe Calculations app, administrators can select Specification Price as the price source and define the new Attribute for Unit Price and Attribute for Price Unit fields to specify where the system retrieves pricing information from the specifications assigned to formula items.

In the Manage Recipes app, product developers can now use Specification Price when viewing Estimated Price calculation results.

This enhancement provides greater flexibility in managing recipe cost calculations by allowing price information to be sourced directly from product specifications.

[Shows an overview of the changes and UI, as outlined in the text.]

To learn more about the feature, see Configuring Recipe Calculations , Checking Recipe Calculations.

entry.title: How to set up external documents via API for Singapore eInvoices?
entry.content:
You have an external system — a third-party ERP, a legacy billing platform, or even an SAP system not yet integrated with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance — that generates electronic invoices in Singapore. You need to submit these invoices to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) or send them to customers via the InvoiceNow/Peppol network, all through SAP Document and Reporting Compliance. The question is: how do you bridge these two worlds?SAP Document and Reporting Compliance now supports External Documents for Singapore. Your external system can upload invoice XML files into SAP DRC using the gco_external REST API, and SAP DRC handles the compliance submission end-to-end. In this blog, I'll walk you through the setup steps — from SAP Note implementation to system configuration, testing, and monitoring.

Get to know about Singapore GST InvoiceNow requirement, and Singapore Peppol eInvoice (InvoiceNow). please check the blog

 GST InvoiceNow - submission of invoice data to Singapore Tax Authority

SAP Document and Reporting Compliance for Singapore Peppol eInvoices (InvoiceNow)

 

Supported Scenarios

The following Singapore e-invoicing scenarios are supported through External Documents:

Scenario

Description

1A — Peppol Customer Invoice

Send a Peppol customer invoice to a customer or IRAS via InvoiceNow / Peppol Network

1B — Peppol Supplier Invoice to IRAS

Submit a Peppol supplier invoice to IRAS

2A/2B — Non-Peppol Customer Invoice to IRAS

Submit a customer invoice (non-Peppol) to IRAS

3A/3B — Non-Peppol Supplier Invoice to IRAS

Submit a supplier invoice (non-Peppol) to IRAS

Note: For detailed XML sample files for all four scenarios, refer to SAP Note 3840047 — Electronic Invoice Processing for Singapore: Preparation of External Documents XML Files.

 

Prerequisites

Before starting, ensure the following are in place:

  • SAP S/4HANA On-Premise (S4CORE 102 or higher) or SAP ERP (SAP_APPL 606, 617, or 618)
  • You have implemented Singapore DRC solution Notes.
  • SSL/TLS is configured on your SAP system
  • Your external system can call REST APIs

 

Part 1: SAP Note Implementation

SAP provides two separate SAP Notes for the Singapore External Documents feature, covering different submission scenarios. Implement the one(s) relevant to your business requirements.

SAP Note

Scenario

3752090

Submitting eInvoices to IRAS

3776506

Sending Peppol eInvoices to customers via InvoiceNow

Step 1: Implement SAP Note 3752090 (Submission to IRAS)

Go to transaction SNOTE. Download and implement SAP Note 3752090.

Step 2: Activate BC Set EDOC_SG_C5_FACTORY_EXT_V3

After implementing the SAP Note, activate the Business Configuration Set that registers the Singapore-specific factory class for External Documents. Go to transaction SCPR20. In the BC Set field, enter EDOC_SG_C5_FACTORY_EXT_V3. Activate it! Note: The Expert Mode flag is required. Without it, the factory class will not be registered correctly for Singapore.

Step 3: Implement SAP Note 3776506 (Peppol Submission to Customers)

Go to transaction SNOTE. Download and implement SAP Note 3776506.

 

Part 2: System Configuration

All configuration below is done via transaction SM30 (Table View Maintenance).

Step 1: Define External Document Systems - Register your external system as a logical system in SAP. Enter view V_TBDLS. Create a new entry and save.

  • Logical System: A unique identifier for your external system (e.g., QKVCLNT440).
  • Name: A meaningful description.

Step 2: Maintain External Document Organizational Unit - Define the organizational unit within your external system that issues invoices. Enter view GCOV_EXT_ORGUNIT. Create a new entry and save.

  • External Document Org. Unit: An identifier for the external organizational unit.
  • External Document Org. Unit Description: A meaningful description.

Step 3: Assign External System and Org Unit to Company Code - Link the external system and org unit to the relevant SAP company code. Enter view GCOV_EXT_ORGCCOD. Create a new entry and save.

Step 4: Assign Process Status to External Document Status - Map external document statuses to SAP eDocument process statuses. Enter view EDOPROCEXTSTATV. Create new entries based on your requirements and save.

Step 5: Verify Factory Class Registration（Only required when you submit eInvoices to IRAS）Confirm that the Singapore factory class has been registered (this should already be in place after activating the BC Set in Step 2). Enter view EDOEXTAPIFACTV. Confirm that an entry exists for country SG (Singapore) with the correct factory class name.

eDoc. Process

Factory Class

Scenario

SGC5INV

CL_EDOC_EXT_DOC_API_SG_C5

Invoice submission to IRAS (C5)

Step 6: Activate EXT_DOC Source Type per Company Code Activate the EXT_DOC source type for each relevant company code. Without this step, the eDocument framework will reject all external documents. Enter view EDOCOMPANYACTIV. Find the entry for your Singapore company code (e.g., SG01). Ensure the Active checkbox is checked for source type EXT_DOC.

 

Part 3: API for External Documents

For a detailed description of the API calls, please refer to the SAP Help Portal. In this blog, I will share an example of calling the Create External Document API using Bruno.

Payload:

{

  "logicalSystemID": "QKVCLNT440",

  "countryRegion": "SG",

  "externalDocuments": [

    {

      "externalOrgUnit": "SG_C5_TEST_ORG_UNIT",

      "externalDocumentType": "CUSTOMER_INVOICE",

      "externalDocumentSubType": "B2B",

      "externalDocumentKey": "EXTDOCAZ2026102801",

      "contentParts": [

        {

          "partType": "main",

          "partID": "PART1A"

        }

      ]

    }

  ]

}

Send request

Check in Transaction EDOC_COCKPIT or Manage Electronic Documents Fiori App

Note: Different externalDocumentType and externalDocumentSubType are required for different scenarios as below.

Scenario

externalDocumentType

externalDocumentSubType

1A — Peppol Customer Invoice

CUSTOMER_INVOICE

B2B

2A/2B — Non-Peppol Customer Invoice to IRAS

CUSTOMER_INVOICE

B2B_EMAIL

1B — Peppol Supplier Invoice to IRAS

SUPPLIER_INVOICE

B2B

3A/3B — Non-Peppol Supplier Invoice to IRAS

SUPPLIER_INVOICE

B2B_EMAIL

 

Part 4: Monitoring in SAP

After submission, you can track the document's processing lifecycle in SAP through two options.

Option 1: eDocument Cockpit (Transaction EDOC_COCKPIT)

  1. Run transaction EDOC_COCKPIT.
  2. Filter by country SG to find your Singapore external documents.
  3. Review the processing status. Double-click a document to see details, AIF messages, and the raw XML payload.

Option 2: Manage Electronic Documents (Fiori App)

  1. Open the Manage Electronic Documents SAP Fiori app.
  2. Filter by country Singapore.
  3. Review statuses, drill into individual documents, and trigger resubmissions if needed.

 

Summary

Here's what you've configured end-to-end:

  1. SAP Note 3752090 implemented (IRAS submission),BC Set EDOC_SG_C5_FACTORY_EXT_V3 activated/SAP Note 3776506 implemented (Peppol submission to customers)
  2. External system registered as logical system, org unit defined, and assigned to company code
  3. Status mapping and factory class verified
  4. bgRFC destination, HTTP service, SSL, certificate mapping, and AIF all enabled
  5. External system ready to POST UBL XML invoices to SAP and have them submitted to IRAS or customers via InvoiceNow/Peppol

I hope this blog post was useful for you! If you have questions or run into issues during your setup, feel free to leave a comment below.

Related Resources

  • SAP Note 3752090 — Electronic Invoice Processing for Singapore: Support for External Documents
  • SAP Note 3840047 — Electronic Invoice Processing for Singapore: Preparation of External Documents XML Files
  • SAP Note 3776506 — Electronic Invoice Processing for Singapore: New API-Based Approach for Submitting Electronic Invoices Created in External Systems
  • SAP Help Portal: Updates to Submitting Electronic Invoices Created in External Systems
  • IMDA InvoiceNow Technical Playbook: https://www.imda.gov.sg/how-we-can-help/nationwide-e-invoicing-framework/invoicenow-technical-playbook

entry.title: Joule Studio empowers teams to build trusted, custom agentic solutions
entry.content:
At SAP Sapphire 2026, we introduced the new Joule Studio and shared our vision of a fully reimagined, AI-first development environment. This week at SAP TechEd, we put Joule Studio in the spotlight to show exactly what kind of agentic solutions you can build. As Chief Product Officer, I’m excited to share more about how Joule Studio changes what’s possible for every team in your organization.

For a business team, this means describing a problem in plain language and getting a governed, production-ready agent, not a slide deck about one. For a developer, it means the same thing, from your own terminal, with full control over the code. For the organizations, it means every one of those agents lands in the same runtime, under the same governance, whether a business user built it in a browser or a platform engineer built it in the terminal.

In this post, I’ll share more about what you can do in Joule Studio, what agentic development looks like, how to create your first agents, and a look ahead at what’s still coming.

Note: General availability for Joule Studio is now underway in a phased approach. Availability expands progressively across customer segments and regions.

What are Joule Studio’s core capabilities?

Joule Studio is a core piece of the SAP Business AI Platform, the AI-native foundation that brings together SAP's deep process and industry knowledge in one place. Joule Studio provides an AI-first development toolkit where builders create agents and workflows that bring the Autonomous Enterprise to life. Here’s a snapshot of what you can build in Joule Studio.

Custom agent creation

Business processes don't wait – approvals stall, data needs chasing, and routine decisions pile up. Too often, the people who should be focused on critical work end up getting stuck managing the coordination. AI agents are designed to absorb exactly that burden: multi-step, adaptive tasks that are too dynamic for traditional automation but too repetitive to deserve human attention every time. This is where Joule Studio comes in.

Joule Studio gives developers and business teams a purpose-built environment for creating custom AI agents, from conversational assistants that respond to user queries to fully autonomous agents that run in the background, triggered by business events or schedules with no human intervention required. Developers can build directly in the Joule Studio web environment or work with the IDE and coding agents they already use, whether it’s VS Code, Claude Code, or Cline, then push code to GitHub and continue right where they left off.

Agents built in Joule Studio are code-based and framework-open, supporting LangGraph, AutoGen, and LlamaIndex, and grounded in your SAP Cloud ERP landscape, so they arrive with native fluency in SAP architecture and data.

n8n workflow generation*

Joule Studio includes a fully managed, embedded n8n environment, bringing visual workflow orchestration directly into SAP Business AI Platform. This means developers can visually orchestrate multi-agent workflows right alongside the agents and applications they're already building without any context switching or separate tooling to manage.

Simply describe your automation need in natural language and Joule Studio generates a production-ready n8n workflow: connecting SAP systems, routing approvals, and triggering downstream actions in the background in response to events or schedules, with no manual coordination required. Since n8n runs on SAP's own cloud infrastructure, rather than as an external SaaS dependency, GDPR and data residency compliance are already baked in.

*n8n is on the roadmap for Q1 2027. Subject to phased rollout.

SAP standard agent extension

SAP ships a growing catalogue of standard agents: for accounts payable, HR, sales, and more. While these are powerful out of the box and they improve with every release, we know that every business runs differently, and there will always be moments where a standard agent needs to know something it doesn't, do something it can't, or hand off to a process that's unique to your organization.

Joule Studio allows you to extend any existing SAP standard agent without touching its core implementation. Currently, you can add your own business logic through custom instructions, and soon you’ll also be able to extend with MCP tools and n8n hooks, which can trigger before or after a workflow execution. Your business logic layers on top while SAP continues to maintain and improve the foundation underneath.

Let’s say your SAP Accounts Payable agent handles invoice matching for most cases automatically. But when matching fails, whether it’s a PO mismatch, a missing goods receipt, or a vendor discrepancy, the standard agent has nowhere to go. With Joule Studio’s agent extension, you’ll be able to attach an after-processing hook that fires precisely at that moment, triggering an n8n workflow to route the exception for manual review, notify the right team, and log the outcome for audit. The AP agent stays standard and maintainable, while your organization's escalation process gets enforced automatically every time.

Collaboration across teams

One of the persistent friction points in enterprise AI development is the handoff between the people who understand the business problem and the people who build the solution. Joule Studio is designed to eliminate that gap. The entire intent-based development workflow (more on that below) is designed to be traceable and shareable.

Joule Studio allows teams to collaborate in a shared workspace for business teams and developers. Builders can share their solutions (whether it’s an agent or workflow) across the team for review and editing, as well as transfer ownership to another team member.

Once a solution is built, sharing it is just as straightforward. Code is pushed to GitHub, making it immediately accessible to any developer on the team to review, extend, or continue building in their IDE of choice. And when it's ready for production, a single deployment step registers the agent or workflow in Joule Work, the engagement layer where end users interact with it, and in SAP AI Agent Hub, where it becomes visible and manageable to IT and operations teams. From the first conversation about a business problem to the moment an end user can act on it, the entire process runs in one connected environment.

Grounding in key business data

An AI agent that can't reliably access your business data isn't solving problems, it's guessing. Getting that grounding right is where most generic development platforms fall short. Joule Studio is built differently, because it's built inside the SAP ecosystem. Every agent created in Joule Studio is grounded in several layers of live enterprise context:

  • SAP Knowledge Graph provides a semantic map of your business: customers, orders, invoices, materials, and how they all connect.
  • SAP Domain Models are trained on the architecture patterns underpinning 77% of global commerce, giving agents native fluency in SAP's own code and data structures before a single line of custom code is written. (Roadmap item for Q1 2027)
  • Process Insights from SAP Signavio surface your actual process models, where time is lost, where errors occur, where the bottlenecks are. (Roadmap item for Q4 2026)
  • Architecture Context from SAP LeanIX maps your live IT landscape, including what's connected, what's on the roadmap, and what needs to stay clean core.
  • Real operational data flows in from day one, pulled directly from your SAP systems and third-party integrations via SAP Business Data Cloud. (Roadmap item for Q4 2026)

What does this mean in practice? Agents can connect natively to your SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, pull HR data from SAP SuccessFactors, or procurement data from SAP Ariba. From day one, they understand the business they’re deployed in, meaning the outputs are more accurate, and the decisions reflect the actual state of your enterprise.

Governance and observability

The faster you scale AI agents across an enterprise, the more urgent a different question becomes: how do you actually know what they're doing and if they’re working correctly? Governance isn't a ‘nice-to-have' at enterprise scale. It’s what makes running agents at scale possible.

Joule Studio builds this in from the start. Before an agent ever reaches production, it goes through a native evaluation framework that assesses quality across two dimensions: technical (is the agent running correctly) and business (is it delivering value). Offline evals for custom agents are sandboxed, isolated from production systems, so testing never causes unintended side effects in live environments.

The moment an agent is deployed, it's automatically registered in the SAP AI Agent Hub, a central command center where IT and operations teams can see every agent running across the enterprise, SAP-built or custom. The Hub maintains a live registry of agents, LLMs, and MCP servers. It also links each one to the business capabilities, processes, and data it touches, and provides drill-down access to execution traces and individual decision logs.

Observability in Joule Studio goes deeper than dashboards. After you've successfully deployed, Joule Studio uses a Git-based CI/CD pipeline to move agent deployments from development to production, with SAP Cloud ALM providing visibility into deployed agent usage, costs, and business impact. At the infrastructure level, every agent runs inside an isolated, managed service powered by NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform, with configurable policies and guardrails that prevent unchecked access to sensitive systems.

Intent-Based Development: Guide to Build Your First Agent

Most development processes face a gap between the person who understands the problem and the person who has to solve it. Joule Studio’s intent-based development flips that model. You start by describing a business outcome, not a technical specification, and the platform generates the artifacts to deliver it. The same process that previously took weeks of coordination and manual work can now happen in minutes to hours, end to end.

And it works however your team works. In Joule Studio, you can create solutions through the web-based UI or running the Joule Studio CLI in your own terminal or whichever AI coding agent you prefer. Both business experts and developers move through the same steps, generate the same artifacts, and land in the same place. Here’s how the process looks:

  1. Business intent: Everything starts with a description in natural language. In the web UI, this is a prompt in the builder. In the CLI, it's the same prompt, typed directly in your IDE. If you want to move fast, add fast track and Joule Studio skips the clarifying questions and gets straight to generating. If the problem is more complex, the iterative path walks you through a structured conversation to make sure nothing gets missed before generation begins.
  2. Requirements: Once your intent is captured, Joule Studio generates a full Product Requirements Document that’s structured, team-readable, and grounded in your actual business context. It incorporates your process models from SAP Signavio, pulls architecture constraints from SAP LeanIX, and references SAP Domain Models to make sure the requirements reflect not just what you described, but how your business actually runs. In the web UI, you review and refine it directly in the builder. In the CLI, it lands as a markdown file in your project you can open, edit, and commit.
  3. Specification: The approved PRD feeds directly into a technical specification, including architecture design, component breakdown, API discovery via the SAP Knowledge Graph, integration patterns, and data models. If an existing MCP server already covers the APIs you need, the spec points to it. The spec is the handoff that makes sure what gets built is what was agreed.
  4. Solution: With the spec confirmed, Joule Studio generates the solution and the actual code. Depending on what you're building, this might be a Python-based AI agent, n8n workflow, MCPs, or a combination. The code follows SAP product standards by default: security, accessibility, performance, and integration patterns are built in, not bolted on afterward. In the web UI, you can preview the running solution immediately. In the CLI, the generated code appears directly in your IDE, ready to inspect, extend, or customize before you do anything else.
  5. Testing: Before anything reaches production, Joule Studio generates test artifacts alongside the solution code, including evals that validate the agent's behavior against the intent it was built to fulfill. In the web UI, evaluations are accessible directly from the agent builder. In the CLI, the test suite is part of the generated project and runs locally in your environment.
  6. Deployment: When you're ready, deployment is a single step. In the web UI, one click moves your solution from the builder into the Joule Studio/SAP-managed runtime, with provisioning, scaling, and lifecycle management handled automatically. In the CLI, a single command does the same thing. Either way, the deployed agent is immediately registered in SAP AI Agent Hub, available for preview, accessible through Joule Work, and observable from day one.

What Comes Next for Joule Studio?

We built Joule Studio because the gap between a good AI idea and a governed, production-ready solution was costing enterprises momentum they could not afford to lose. Looking ahead, here’s a sneak peek at what you can expect from Joule Studio:

  • BDC data products: With BDC integration, you’ll be able to close the loop between your data and agents. Joule Studio will enable building custom derived data products directly from the Studio, then let agents query and reason over them as live structured sources, all without leaving your development environment.
  • CAP and Vercel app generation: Beyond agents and workflows, Joule Studio will extend its intent-based generation to full-stack enterprise applications. This includes SAP CAP-powered backends with data models and APIs, and Vercel-generated modern web frontiers, so teams can build every layer of a solution from the same intent-driven workflow.
  • Advanced observability: We're expanding what it means to understand your agents in production, with cost attribution, performance trends, and anomaly detection that give teams not just a view of what's happening, but the data to act on it.
  • SAP Build transition: Customers and partners who have built on SAP Build and Joule Studio, classic edition will receive guided transition support to move their projects to Joule Studio incrementally, at their own pace, protecting the investments they have already made while opening the door to everything the new platform offers.

entry.title: Can You Run a Space Station? Lessons on Sustainability from the Dubai Museum of the Future
entry.content:
The Metaphor of the Orbiting Outpost
If you step onto Level 2 of the Dubai Museum of the Future, you will encounter the OSS Hope Simulator from SAP. Set against a glowing, interactive console, it presents users with a direct challenge: "Can you run a space station?"
 
To enterprise architects, developers, and consultants, this installation is far more than a visionary gaming experience. A space station operates as a strictly closed system. There is no margin for error; every drop of water, molecule of carbon, and unit of energy must be meticulously logged, tracked, and reused.
This setup mirrors our situation on Earth. Our planet is a closed ecosystem facing finite resource boundaries. The exhibit emphasizes that the exact same real-time data tracking required to sustain life in space is essential to preserving our enterprise ecosystems on Earth.
 
The Three Pillars of a Circular Enterprise
The logic of the simulator relies on keeping three core metrics balanced. These variables map directly to SAP's foundational sustainability pillars:
  • Zero Emissions: Moving beyond simple carbon estimation to active, automated decarbonization across the entire supply chain.
  • Zero Waste: Shifting production models from linear consumption to fully circular material loops where nothing is discarded.
  • Zero Inequalities: Establishing transparent workforce safety, ethical sourcing, and corporate governance down to the last tier of suppliers.
In a space station, you cannot survive without a central ledger to balance these vectors. On Earth, you cannot optimize what you do not accurately count.
 
️ Decoding the Architecture behind the "Wall of Knowledge"
The installation features an interactive "Wall of Knowledge" that showcases real-world global use cases. The simulator's backend logic runs on eight distinct technology domains. Five of these domains form the core foundation of the SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) ecosystem:
 
1. Embedded AI & Predictive Forecasting
  • Simulation Mechanics: Dynamically balancing oxygen reserves and predicting machinery failure points before they occur.
  • SAP Enterprise Deployment: Embedding native intelligence via SAP Business AI and SAP Joule to flag supply chain anomalies, forecast emissions spikes, and automate ledger corrections before period-end close.
2. Advanced Real-Time Analytics
  • Simulation Mechanics: Aggregating and visualizing live telemetry across life support, energy grids, and cargo bays.
  • SAP Enterprise Deployment: Ingesting highly disparate IoT and operational data into the high-speed data tier of SAP HANA. This feeds directly into an auditable ESG reporting layer via the SAP Sustainability Control Tower.
 
3. Digital Twins & Simulation Sandboxes
  • Simulation Mechanics: Testing the operational risk of environmental adjustments inside a safe virtual environment first.
  • SAP Enterprise Deployment: Mapping asset management data to live logistics feeds. This allows operations leads to simulate structural facility changes before committing physical resources.
4. Blockchain & Asset Traceability
  • Simulation Mechanics: Verifying the origin, safety, and operational lifecycle of all arriving raw materials.
  • SAP Enterprise Deployment: Utilizing immutable ledger records to verify end-to-end supply chain transparency, ensuring strict compliance with evolving international sustainability regulations.
5. Hyper-Automation
  • Simulation Mechanics: Executing real-time automated adjustments to life support loops to completely eliminate human delay.
  • SAP Enterprise Deployment: Orchestrating touchless business workflows across SAP S/4HANA to dynamically adjust production rates based on resource availability.
The Enterprise Lesson: Profit and Planet on a Single Platform
The ultimate takeaway for the SAP ecosystem is clear: the precision engineering needed to pilot a space station matches the exact methodology required to run a sustainable business.
As technology professionals, the configurations, custom code lines, and system integrations we build on SAP BTP serve as the actual plumbing for global resource consumption. By integrating carbon, waste, and social ledgers directly into our core ERP data structures, we turn abstract sustainability goals into repeatable, daily business operations.

entry.title: What makes process management so valuable? Making interface problems tangible
entry.content:
All of us in this community use SAP in teaching from different perspectives, and I always find it exciting to read how, with which different learning objectives, and in which learning contexts SAP is used.

Of course, I am particularly interested in where colleagues who teach in the same area as I do—namely process management and ERP systems—place their emphasis and what experiences they have with designing exercises.

So that I am not only benefiting from others, I am also happy to share one or another experience from my lectures on process management and ERP systems.

In this lecture, I convey the fundamentals of E2E processes, show how these tasks are handled one after another across different departments, what interests the individual departments have, and I also discuss with the students goal conflicts or possible communication problems between the departments at the interfaces. To illustrate such an E2E process, I also make use of the opportunity to have the students execute the complete process in SAP and assume different roles within this process. The process starts with a customer order, goes through an MRP run, the procurement of raw materials, production processing (two-stage), delivery, billing, and ends with the receipt of payment. As Matt Dyki has already mentioned in his post, the students have the unique opportunity to get to know the process completely in different roles.

This learning experience is the basis for the students to be able to somehow understand this buzzword “end-to-end process.” For us instructors, a major task is to make all these buzzwords—which are very abstract and, for students who have never been in a company, hardly understandable—tangible and experiential.

Now the students know the overall sequence and can also understand quite well how the tasks are connected. But have they thereby already experienced what process management is all about? Have the students been able to experience how valuable it is to have an overview of the entire process flow?

My assumption was: rather not. Each student essentially handled this process on their own and at most had problems with execution in SAP, but did not experience and did not feel what possible communication problems at the interfaces could mean.

I explained it and saw that the students made an effort to understand what I mean when I describe and explain this fundamental issue to them. But I wanted to make this problem tangible for the students.

We now simulate this process run as in a company, and the students experience and feel what communication problems are, what interfaces between departments are—and how important an understanding of processes is.

The exercise itself is quite simple. After the students have become familiar with all tasks within the complete process flow, we replicate the situation as it is in a company. We form individual classic departments, such as Purchasing, Sales, Production Planning, Production, Financial Accounting, etc., each responsible only for its specific task. For this, we always have two to three students in a department. Each group receives a precise task description that builds on the tasks of the E2E process. That is, we use the same APPS and the same master data.

The task for everyone is now to process as many processes as possible from order to incoming payment within three hours. We have a benchmark that currently stands at 16 complete processes.

Don’t be afraid of chaos!

You might now be saying this won’t work. I say: endure the chaos at the beginning. The students need a little time to understand the idea of the exercise and to organize themselves. After that, all groups so far have participated with great eagerness and enjoyment.

The instructor functions only as a coach and mainly helps at the beginning and explains when questions arise.

In the following session, we evaluate the processes. Where were the bottlenecks? At which point did particularly many processes get stuck, or where were there long waiting times, and what were the causes?

Would you like to try this as well? I would be happy to exchange ideas or further develop the idea.

Best regards

Uta Mathis

Business Process Management and ERP-Systems

Department Business and Engineering

Hochschule Esslingen – University of Applied Sciences, Germany

entry.title: Co-Teaching Across the Globe? Exploring the Potential of COIL Projects
entry.content:
Perhaps you’ve already heard of it: co-teaching or a COIL project? What is a COIL project? Freie Universität Berlin defines it as follows: A COIL project (Collaborative Online International Learning) is an international, digital teaching and learning format that virtually connects students and instructors from different countries.

The idea is to find a colleague who either has a complementary topic or the same topic, and we teach reciprocally in each other’s courses.

The scope ranges from a single session to an entire lecture over a full semester, or even up to curricular integration.

For students, it can be exciting to get to know students from another university, to learn about a different higher education system and other cultures, and—if English is not their native language—to communicate with other students in that language.

As instructors, you have the opportunity to incorporate different emphases into your lecture, learn from your co-teaching partner, and gain new experiences.

Why am I posting this here in the SAP Community? There are universities that have their own departments whose task is to find suitable matches between their own instructors and those at other universities. My thought is: we already have a matching pool here—why not use it? We work in the areas of business processes, ERP systems, AI, low-code, no-code … and we do this “all over the world.”

Of course, there are a few peripheral issues we need to clarify, such as finding suitable time slots, aligning on topics, and clarifying the technical setup, like how to join and how collaboration will work. But we can start small.

In my Business Process Management course, together with a colleague from the US, I designed and delivered five joint sessions. We had one joint session in which the project idea, the goal, and the framework were presented, and all participants briefly introduced themselves. Then my colleague led two sessions on change management, which always fits well with process management, and I covered the topic of process modeling in BPMN, also in two sessions.

Change management was discussed using a case study that was provided in advance and had to be worked through. Guidelines and fundamentals of process management were likewise provided and explained again during the session, and open questions were clarified. After that, the students—working in mixed groups—had the task of documenting a process familiar to students at both universities, such as exam registration, identifying differences and similarities, and deriving an idea for best practice from that.

The feedback from both sides—both from the students and from the instructors—was very positive. In particular, the cultural differences and the different approaches to learning were perceived by students on both sides as enriching.

For my colleague and me, it was a great experience that we are happy to share and continue. However, my colleague will soon be retiring.

I would be glad to carry out another co-teaching or COIL project on the topic of business process management or processes in ERP systems.

If you’re interested, please get in touch. If you have questions about the structure or the organization, you are likewise invited to reach out. If you’re looking for partners on specific topics, you can also use this chat to submit requests or post offers.

I look forward to a lively discussion on this topic.

Uta Mathis

Hochschule Esslingen – University of Applied Sciences, Germany

Working outdoors or in a lower-light environment? Which display mode works best for you?

The SAP Field Service and Asset Management mobile app now comes with two display modes: dark mode and light mode.
