entry.title: Re: ABAP Debugger Enhancement — Reloaded: Typed VALUE Statements and What's Changed Since 2019
entry.content:
Thanks a lot for the kind words and the great question!

Capturing complex business scenarios as regression test data is exactly the
use case the tool was built for. Thanks again for the feedback!

Short answer: DDVE does not support reference components today, and there is
no mechanism to reconstruct them. The current behaviour, verified in the code:
reference components are either left out of the generated statement or, in
some constellations, stop the rendering with a visible marker. Neither is a
deliberate design decision yet, it is simply a case the tool has never handled
explicitly.

On the design side I see it like this: a VALUE #( ... ) literal can only carry
data. Object references (REF TO object) are out of scope by design, because
reconstructing an instance would require its full internal state and the
constructor semantics. In a unit test that is exactly where a test double
belongs. Data references (REF TO data) are different: they could be rendered as
NEW typ( ... ) or REF #( ... ) around the dereferenced content. That is not
implemented yet but technically feasible.

entry.title: Component Scrap from SAP Digital Manufacturing POD 2.0
entry.content:
Introduction

Imagine an operator halfway through an order. They pick up a component and it is clearly no good, cracked, expired, or damaged in handling. The sensible thing is to scrap it then and there and carry on. However, SAP Digital Manufacturing currently don´t support component, floor stock, inventory scrap from PODs out of the box.

How SAP Digital Manufacturing handles this today

Out of the box, scrapping floor stock is done in a separate app called Manage Floor Stocks. The steps are straightforward, they just live outside the POD:

- Open the Manage Floor Stocks app.
- Find the Inventory ID you want to scrap.
- Edit that stock record.
- Decrease the Quantity on Hand by entering the Quantity to Adjust.
- Choose the reason code SCR-SCRAP and save.

Check Floor Stock Return and Scrap for more details.

For an inventory clerk that is perfectly fine. For an operator in the middle of execution it means leaving the POD, switching into a general maintenance app, and finding the way back. In practice the scrap often gets postponed, and postponed scrap is how on hand numbers quietly drift away from reality.

What I built

The Scrap Inventory plugin is a POD 2.0 widget that puts the scrap action inside PODs.

The flow is about as short as it gets: search a material, look at its stock, type a quantity, scrap.

What it does

  • Material search with value help. Type a material, or click Browse to open a picker that shows only materials that actually have inventory in the plant.
  • Friendly search. The picker does instant substring search, so typing DRILL finds DRILL-TIP. No need to remember exact codes.
  • A clear stock view. For the chosen material you see every stock line: Inventory ID, quantity on hand with its unit of measure, material, version, description, and storage location.
  • Partial or full scrap per Inventory ID. Enter a quantity on any line and confirm. The widget checks it against what is on hand, posts the scrap, confirms success, and refreshes the list.

Only ERP origin, scrap eligible stock is shown, so there are no dead ends.

Why it is nice to have

  • The operator never leaves the POD. The action happens where the work happens.
  • Fewer clicks. One quantity entry replaces the open app, find, edit, adjust, reason code, save sequence.
  • Fewer mistakes. Only eligible stock is listed, and quantities are validated before anything is posted.
  • A focused screen. Operators get a single purpose scrap action instead of a full inventory maintenance app and the wider permissions that come with it.
  • Accurate numbers. The scrap posts through the standard SAP Digital Manufacturing inventory API, so on hand stock and the postings behind it stay correct.

Try it yourself

Check Scrap Inventory custom POD 2.0 plugin on GitHub.

The repository has the full widget source, translations for the supported SAP DM languages, a ready to deploy package, and step by step install instructions.

Conclusion

This is a small plugin that removes a daily bit of friction. Operators scrap in the moment, by the person who spotted the problem, and inventory stays trustworthy as a result. 

Disclaimer: This is a community extension and is not officially supported by SAP. Use at your own discretion.

Do you want to see more content like this? Please live a Like!

Best,
Manoel Costa

entry.title: Re: Outbound Delivery OdataV2 api to Creates outbound del...
entry.content: In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the creation operation of API API_OUTBOUND_DELIVERY_SRV does not support populating all delivery execution fields during outbound delivery creation. Fields such as Storage Location and Batch are determined by standard delivery processing and are not available as creatable attributes in the delivery creation payload. Therefore, these values cannot be provided directly in the POST request. They must either be determined automatically by standard logic or maintained through a subsequent update process/API if supported. Additionally, the metadata document should be checked to verify the exact list of creatable properties and the required date format for PlannedGoodsIssueDate.

It remains a very general question and, in my view, it is difficult to answer it in detail, as each individual case must always be examined.

In my experience, things have always been complicated when third-party systems (for example, in production) process SAP data via an interface and send it back to SAP. In such cases, you should plan to carry out a detailed analysis of the process and data flows in advance, followed by extensive testing. This will help to avoid project delays.
